prompt: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art sprite concept for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: a single DEPTH MINE enemy of the Iron Tide, a sleeping naval contact mine from the black-blue abyss, isolated. A round heavy sphere hull in near-black blue-gray iron, with a cool deep-teal rim highlight along its top-left and an equator seam of small rivets. Eight short stubby contact spikes stick straight out evenly around its silhouette, each a little cylinder horn with a pale steel cap. In the center of its face a single round eye-light glows bright cyan with a white pupil-spark, set in a dark recessed socket ring, staring forward. From the bottom hangs a short gunmetal anchor chain of four or five oval links ending in a small weight. A few tiny pale cyan bioluminescent specks dot the hull. Round, spiky, instantly readable silhouette. Side view facing left, the whole mine and chain centered with a generous empty margin on all sides on a perfectly flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background that fills the whole image. Crisp chunky pixel art with a 1-pixel near-black navy outline at the sprite's native pixel scale, flat saturated fills with three-step shading ramps lit from the top-left, bold simple shape that stays readable at small size, no anti-aliasing, no seabed, no water, no bubbles, no scenery, no stars, no cast shadow, no glow bleeding onto the background, no text, no labels.
